A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TIMEOMNI-VL work. All 27 pages of v1 and 30 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting, imputation, understanding and reasoning results, alongside representation and understanding-model ablations and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds controlled baseline comparisons, TIME benchmark evaluations, representation ablations and variable-order robustness results.

M1.justification: The Bagel-based architecture, Bi-TSI conversion, RFN, capacity constraints, CoT conditioning and training losses remain unchanged. The new resolution and color variants are experimental ablations, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix E.4.2 adds evaluation on external TIME benchmark subsets for forecasting and imputation, retaining the existing task families and GIFT-Eval/TSR-Suite coverage. The TIME subset composition is unspecified, so additional domain or population coverage cannot be established.

E2.justification: v2 adds VisionTS++ to the GIFT-Eval imputation comparison in Table 9; it was absent from v1's imputation comparison. Existing main-table, understanding and reasoning comparator sets remain unchanged. VisionTS++ retraining settings are separately relevant to E3.

E3.justification: The original evaluation protocols remain intact. Added experiments introduce VisionTS++ retraining on the same 5k generation samples, 224/448/896 image resolutions, single-color inference and fine-tuning, and permutation testing on 200 multivariate examples per generation task. These are additional protocols rather than replacements for the original settings.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.5 substantially extends analysis of the representation: Table 12 tests resolution versus accuracy and computational cost, Table 13 tests dependence on color cues, and Table 14 tests sensitivity to variable ordering. The original heatmap and understanding-model ablations and appendix case studies are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without repeated-run uncertainty. v2's Table 14 adds three shuffled evaluation groups alongside original ordering, plus means and 95% confidence intervals. This is localized uncertainty reporting; additional training seeds or repeated training runs are not established.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1, 2, 7 and 8 retain their numerical results. New Tables 9–14 add substantial comparison, generalization and sensitivity results. Table 9 reports forecasting/imputation averages of 0.826/0.810 for TIMEOMNI-VL versus 0.900/0.827 for retrained VisionTS++; TIME results report averages of 0.858/0.784. These are newly reported comparisons, not demonstrated performance improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, losses, conversion equations, capacity conditions and Appendix C–D derivations are retained. Renaming the periodic-block count and context-length symbols in the main text changes notation rather than mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims about vision-centric unification, Bi-TSI, TSUMM-SUITE and understanding-guided generation. The headline understanding, forecasting, imputation and average 8.2% generation-gain claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix G substantially expands applicability boundaries: understanding tasks and CoT are characterized as task-specific scaffolding, validation is limited to Bagel and modest training data, and efficiency, color dependence and irregular sampling constrain applicability. Appendix E.5 adds interpretations of the new sensitivity tests. Figure 3 also changes 'lossless' to 'near-lossless,' consistent with qualifications already present in v1's Appendix C.

D1.justification: v2 adds code and checkpoint access links and states that these resources are public. Table 12 newly reports per-image training and inference times. Existing hardware, learning rate, warm-up, prompts and conversion implementation descriptions remain substantially unchanged; resource accessibility was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds Qiao et al. (2026) for the TIME benchmark. Most other reference changes update publication details, years or formatting for the same works; the related-work narrative and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are preserved, with localized grammar, terminology and notation edits, updated publication and acknowledgment text, and new appendix subsections. The line-plot discussion moves from E.4 to E.6 without substantive rewriting.

P2.justification: New Tables 9–14 substantially expand the experimental displays to cover controlled comparisons, external evaluation, efficiency, rendering ablations and uncertainty. Figures 2–4 receive smaller label or caption corrections, and Table 2 moves to the following page. Existing case-study tables are retained and renumbered from 9–18 to 15–24.

improvement.justification: The matched-data baseline comparison and representation tests strengthen support for the existing design, while Appendix G and resource links improve transparency. The gain remains limited by unspecified TIME subset composition and incomplete explanation of settings behind the new ablation reference scores, which differ from the unchanged main results. Overall, v2 provides useful additional validation and better-calibrated limitations without fully resolving those reporting gaps.
